The paper and the control are different editions

Two of those rows are not numbering artefacts — they are real differences in the program.

  • The control has two nets the paper does not (decoded 248 and 249): the Z-balance pump latch, started by X9.6 DEC7 and stopped by X9.7 DEC8, with a TB36 run timeout.
  • The paper has one net the control does not (printed N00526): a balance pressure alarm raised straight off X1009.7 DEC8 into A6.2, alarm 1026.

So the Z-balance logic was reworked after the listing was printed — which fits a machine with K7.3 = 1, where Y3.5 is committed to the balance pump. Where the two disagree, the binary is what the machine runs.

One consequence is worth knowing at the machine: alarm 1026 can no longer fire. A6.2 has no coil anywhere in the loaded ladder. Its text is still in the message table and net N00171 still reads it as an interlock, so a stuck bit would still block the arm — but nothing sets it. See Machine alarms.

Instruction names

Ten were read straight off the listing: END1, MOVE, COIN, XMOV, ADD, SUB, NUME, TMRB, NUMEB, SPE. Those anchor FANUC's standard numbering, which supplies the rest. Four more were resolved from how they behave:

SUBNameEvidence
41DISPBone parameter, the value 200, gated on NOT NOALM — a message-display scan of the A area, which holds 208 message bits
65CALLfour call sites whose identifiers match those carried by END2 and the three SPEs; FANUC puts CALL at 65, seven before the confirmed SPE at 72
36ADDBbinary arithmetic family: R20 + 5 → R22 with an overflow coil
38MULBsame family: R16 × 10 → R18, and R22 × 10 → R24, feeding G30, the spindle override

SUB 54 and SUB 55 do not exist in this program. They were picked up by the length-discovery pass reading trailing data past the program end at offset 16266, and have been dropped. SUB 59 is the only one still unnamed: two uses, both a masked transfer into the CNC override inputs — R70 → G10 masked 0xFFFF and R18 → G12 masked 0xFF.

Known limits

  • Step numbers are not FANUC's. FANUC counts a functional instruction as several steps; this decode counts instructions. The printed listing's step column runs to about 4 277 where this one reaches 3 902. Cross-reference by net number or symbol, not by step.
  • The +2 band (decoded 572–621) is inferred, not directly verified — OCR coverage of the printed net-number column is thin through the second subprogram. It is bracketed on both sides by verified anchors and the arithmetic closes exactly on 703.
  • Functional-instruction parameters are shown as area addresses only where FANUC's published parameter layout says that position is an address. Everything else is left as the raw number rather than guessed at.
  • Two symbols in the table, ZFGRBX and APC, sit at addresses no instruction references — dead entries from another build.

See Ladder listing for the program itself, PMC address map for the symbol table, and M functions — what the ladder does for what came out of it.

Open items

15. Reference

Things that need a look at the machine or an answer from a supplier.

Check at the control

  1. C1 and C2 counter presets against 24 pockets. SYSTEM → PMC → PMCPRM → COUNTER. The backup holds 36. See Magazine and tool table.
  2. SRAM size at the boot screen. Power on holding the two right-most soft keys. Decides whether the memory upgrade is already installed. See Memory.
  3. Parameter 1010 reads 4 while 9900 reads 3. Read both.
  4. Is Y9 genuinely undriven? Watch it on PMCDGN → STATUS before using it. See Spare capacity.

Check on the machine

  1. ZF gearbox model — read the plate. 2K15 and 2K20 have the selector motor alongside on a worm shaft; 2K10 and 2K12 have it on top under a plastic cover. Decides the oil fill and the clutch torque spec.
  2. Is a spindle or gearbox cooler physically fitted? The build sheet ticks 68K04 cooling; K006.2 says no PMC-controlled spindle cooler.
  3. Are terminals 112–119 landed in the pendant? The drawing shows the pins with names struck through, which means unassigned — not necessarily unterminated.
  4. X4.6 — the ladder calls it ESKIP1, one drawing revision says SPARE and another says HANDLE ENABLE. Ring it out before using it.
  5. Main CPU board edition — the data sheet says A16B-3200-0210 edition 05C. Confirm before ordering a SIMM.

Ask a supplier

  1. FANUC — will they still write options for a 2001 18-C? Quote serial E00905277, and ask for J802#4 and J802#5 pricing together.
  2. Memex — confirm the real memory ceiling on BDB1 Ver 0025. Their note says 1280 m; their introduction implies 1920 m.
  3. Renishaw — request O9818, and the definition of #120 for this control. See Probing macro suites.

Unresolved in the documents

  • Alarm 1015 is referenced by the operation manual but carries no message text in the ladder.
  • D002–D005 spindle speed settings do not decode cleanly as rpm and the byte order is not stated.
  • Eight enabled option bits land on rows the tables leave blank — 9924.2, 9925.2, 9928.7, 9933.2, 9944.5, 9945.7, 9946.0, 9953.7.
  • Keep relays K003.7, K006.5 and K017.4 are set but undefined in Johnford's table.
  • The operation box is listed as a 10.4 in LCD by Johnford and an 8.4 in LCD/MDI by FANUC.

Closed by the ladder decode

  • Y9 undriven — confirmed across all 699 nets; the byte is free.
  • Symbols outside the verified areas — all resolved; only two dead symbols remain, ZFGRBX and APC, at addresses no instruction references.
  • D2–D5 spindle speed settings — they are not rpm. They are three canned serial-spindle commands the PMC substitutes for override, gear change and door interlock. See Ladder audit.
  • Alarm 1015 — it does have message text (X / Y axis machine lock); what it lacks is a coil. Four others are in the same position.
  • M20, M24, M37, M39 — traced to their coils. See M functions.

Added by the ladder audit

  • T40 = 0 ms — the only delay on alarm 1004 for the fast-arm path. Read it on the TIMER screen.
  • C1 / C2 current = 6 — a 2001 snapshot of the magazine position. It must match where the magazine physically sits before the first tool change.
  • Stored stroke limits 1320 / 1321 — the only travel protection there is; nothing else will stop the axes.
  • Terminal 158 — may be ESKIP1 rather than a spare input. Ring it out before wiring a probe to it.
  • X3.6 and X4.5 — used by the ladder, no symbol. Identify from the drawings.
  • Balance pressure — no alarm and no Z interlock in the loaded ladder. Check whether a hardwired path exists.
  • Reference return — the DEC switches are not read by the ladder and no deceleration signal is driven. Watch a reference return to see how it decelerates.
